results.summary: This Wokwi design uses an AND gate to drive a seven-segment LED display so that it shows the digit seven. It is controlled by two input switches, and the documentation says toggling inputs 3 and 4 causes the seven to appear. The only external hardware needed is an LED display. The project is a minimal educational logic example with very little documentation beyond the test instruction.

This Wokwi project implements a full adder using two XOR gates, two AND gates, and an OR gate. Inputs IN0, IN1, and IN2 represent A, B, and carry-in, while OUT0 and OUT1 show the binary sum on LEDs. It is tested by setting the three switches and observing the two output LEDs. The design is a straightforward educational arithmetic-logic example with limited documentation.

This Wokwi design contains one AND gate and one NOT gate for basic logic testing. IN0 and IN1 feed the AND gate whose output is OUT1, while IN2 feeds the NOT gate whose output is OUT2. Testing consists of checking the AND and NOT truth tables against LEDs connected to the outputs. The documentation is thin and the project is a simple classroom-style logic exercise.

This Verilog design contains two numerically controlled oscillators built from phase accumulators and sine lookup tables, with their outputs multiplied together by default. NCO B can be bypassed to a constant one or half, and a boxcar filter can be enabled; tuning ranges at 50 MHz are roughly 0.195 to 24.8 MHz for NCO A and up to 12.3 MHz for NCO B. The output is intended to drive a simple R-2R DAC and be observed on an oscilloscope, and the author warns that high-frequency output will not be clean. It is a compact signal-generation experiment with detailed pin-level control but no silicon test results.

This Wokwi project implements an 8-bit linear-feedback shift register that acts as a pseudo-random number generator. The eight output pins present a pseudo-random 8-bit value roughly once per second, and LEDs can be connected to view the result. The design is based on a published LFSR reference found via web search. Documentation is brief and gives no detail on the tap polynomial or clock source.

This Wokwi design builds NAND-gate equivalents of common logic gates. Six inputs and six outputs are provided, and the test procedure is to apply inputs and verify that the odd-numbered outputs match the even-numbered outputs. External hardware consists of a DIP switch for inputs and LEDs for outputs. The documentation is very sparse and does not list which gates are implemented or how the outputs are paired.

This Wokwi project is described only as using several flip-flops and multiplexers. It exposes eight inputs and eight outputs, and the test instruction is simply to test carefully with LEDs connected to the outputs. No functional description, schematic, or expected behavior is provided. The documentation is too thin to determine what the design actually computes.

This project is an unmodified Tiny Tapeout Wokwi template with placeholder text such as testing 1 2 3 and instructions to explain how the project works. It has two inputs and two outputs and a 1 Hz clock, but no real function is described. The one-line description calls it a broken tatanator2000, and no external hardware is specified. There is essentially no usable documentation.

This Wokwi project is a Tiny Tapeout template used to test an LED digit display. It has eight inputs and eight outputs, and the test procedure is simply to flip switches as desired and observe the LED number. The documentation still contains the template placeholder text for external hardware. It is a minimal display experiment rather than a defined function.

This Wokwi design outputs a number on a seven-segment display corresponding to which input switch is high, so switch 0 shows 1, switch 2 shows 2, and so on. It is tested by turning on switches and checking that the displayed digit matches. External hardware is an LED display and switches. The project is described as the author's first Wokwi design and is a simple educational switch-to-display exercise.
